title: 🏛️ Exams 2013–2026 · the right preposition in exam texts ⭐⭐

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2026, technical) A text tells how Drew Mascotti, a pizza deliverer, became a welder. Which word completes the sentence?
"So, he signed up for a night class ___ a local tech school to see if welding was a skill that 'was going to stick.'"
questions.explanation: The phrase names the place where the course is given, and for a school or an institution as a place of study, English uses "at". "on" and "by" do not name the place of a class, and "before" is a time word: nothing in the sentence says the class came before the school.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2026, general) A text says Hannah's children do not go to school. Which word completes the sentence?
"Instead, they take part ___ 'democratic learning' groups where they make their own rules and decide on homework."
questions.explanation: The expression is "take part in" something: to join an activity or a group. "take part of" copies the idea of being "a part of" a group, which is a different meaning and a different structure, and "at" or "on" do not go with "take part".

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2025, general) A text warns against junk food. Which word completes the sentence?
"Yet, we should not forget that this addiction to junk food can have negative effects ___ our health and well-being."
questions.explanation: We say that something has an effect "on" a person or a thing: the effect falls on our health. "to", "at" and "of" cannot link "effects" to what is affected.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2025, general) A text explains what children learn from household chores. Which word completes the sentence?
"It helps them to learn about what they need to do to care ___ themselves, a home and a family."
questions.explanation: "To care for" someone means to look after them, and it is followed directly by the person or the thing. "of" belongs to the longer expression "take care of", which needs the verb "take"; the sentence has "to care" only. "with" does not follow "care".

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2023, general) A text says children can do more chores than parents think. Which word completes the sentence?
"___ a young age, children are capable of handling more than we may believe."
questions.explanation: For an age, English says "at": "at a young age", "at the age of six". "In" is the preposition for a period such as "in 1997" or "in summer", and "By" would mean "not later than" a given age.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2019, general) A text presents Earth Hour, when lights are turned off for a short time. Which word completes the sentence?
"It proves that even doing a little thing, like turning the lights off ___ one hour can make a little difference."
questions.explanation: The words "one hour" give the length of time the lights stay off, and a length of time is introduced by "for". "from" would need an end point ("from 8 to 9"), "at" names a single moment on the clock, and "about" does not fit before a duration in this sentence.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2021, general) A text lists the health benefits of cycling. Which word completes the sentence?
"Some extra movement as part ___ your daily routine can help you keep fit and healthy."
questions.explanation: We say "part of" something: the extra movement is one piece of the whole daily routine. "for" and "from" cannot link "part" with the whole it belongs to.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2020, technical) A woman tells how she joined her partner's design company. Which word completes the sentence?
"And the rest of the time I'd be with the kids and looking ___ the business from home."
questions.explanation: "Look after" means to take care of something and to run it, which is what she does for the business from home. "look for" would mean to search for it, and "look at" to watch it; neither says that she runs it.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2019, general) A volunteer remembers her first days at a hospital. Which word completes the sentence?
"When I first began volunteering at a hospital, I was very timid and nervous ___ meeting new people."
questions.explanation: The adjective "nervous" is followed by "about" for the thing that worries us, and a preposition is followed by the -ing form: "nervous about meeting". "with" would link the feeling to a person, not to what she has to do.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2019, technical) A text tells how Katie became a lorry driver among men. Which word completes the sentence?
"People laughed ___ her because there were no women doing this job."
questions.explanation: "Laugh at" someone means to make fun of them: the people were mocking her. "laugh of" copies the French "rire de" and "laugh on" does not exist.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2015, technical) A text gives safety advice on eye protection at work. Which word completes the sentence?
"Good equipment can protect your eyes ___ irritation and injuries."
questions.explanation: "Protect something from" a danger means to keep the danger away from it: goggles keep irritation and injuries away from the eyes. "for" would mean the equipment is meant to give irritation, and "of" does not follow "protect".

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2013, general) A text presents Jane Parker, who won a poetry competition at twelve. Which word completes the sentence?
"Her parents were very proud ___ her."
questions.explanation: The adjective "proud" takes "of" for the person or the thing we are proud of: "proud of her". "with" and "at" do not follow "proud".
